title: fix: let fal queue jobs finish and move Stable Audio to the queue
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes the fal billing audit findings where fal ran and billed jobs we had already failed.

- Removes the `runFalJob` poll cap (5 min for the video and image fallbacks, 10 min for 3D). The durable generation alarm bounds the wait, as #15283 did for Wan 3.
- Moves Stable Audio 3 Medium from the blocking `fal.run` route to the fal queue.
- Trade-off: a job fal never finishes now fails at the 15-min alarm limit instead of after 5 min.

| Finding (last 14 days) | fal request log |
|---|---|
| `wan-2.2-fast:fal` 504 "timed out after 300s" ×2 | One finished (200) at 375 s, 75 s after we gave up. The other ran 80 min, then 422. |
| `stable-audio-3-medium` 524 ×2 | Both ran on fal after our 125 s cutoff. One user then retried 5×. |

Findings that need no change here:
- Wan 3 504s: fixed by #15283, none since.
- MiniMax overcharge: deliberate until the fal promo ends Sep 30 (#15413).
- `cost_variant = 'undefined'`: Tinybird's default for an unset string.
- grok-imagine-video gap: fal bills xAI's post-generation rejections, which we never bill. This needs a pricing decision and gets its own PR.

Tests: fal client, fallback and 3D unit tests (32) and both Stable Audio route tests pass. `tsc` is clean.

gist.headline: Let the queue finish buzzing
gist.blurb: fal jobs now get the time their durable queue already promised them. Stable Audio 3 Medium has also moved into the queue, where long-running sound can finish its little song without being cut off at the door.
gist.summary: Removed the 5-minute (and 10-minute 3D) `runFalJob` polling caps so durable fal generations can complete until the 15-minute generation alarm, and moved Stable Audio 3 Medium from blocking `fal.run` to the fal queue.
gist.impact: Image, video, 3D, and Stable Audio requests that take longer than the former 125–300 second cutoffs can now return their completed fal result through the queue, with unfinished work bounded by the 15-minute alarm.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy queue garden represents durable generation work being allowed to bloom instead of being prematurely clipped: Stable Audio is a little retro cassette/speaker plant with musical notes traveling along a clear queue path toward a finished-output terminal. Polli, wearing tiny studio headphones, patiently tends the path while a CRT monitor robot watches the completion light; clocks are present but friendly, showing that the queue has time to finish.
